title: Functional groups: Classification of organic compounds; Measuring enthalpy changes; Energy cycles in reactions

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Hydroxyl group
items.clue: An –OH group covalently bonded to a carbon atom, the functional group of the alcohols (for example CH₃CH₂OH).

items.label: Structural isomers
items.clue: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different connectivities (different sequences of bonded atoms).

items.label: Amido group
items.clue: A carbonyl carbon atom bonded directly to a nitrogen atom, –CONH₂ (or –CONH– and –CON< when the nitrogen carries alkyl groups).

items.label: Phenyl group
items.clue: The group –C₆H₅: a benzene ring bonded to the rest of the molecule through one of its carbon atoms, as in methylbenzene, C₆H₅CH₃.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the temperature of a substance?

options.text: The form of energy that flows from a hot object to a cold one
A measure of the total kinetic energy of all the particles it has
A quantity that has to rise whenever heat is transferred into it
A measure of the average kinetic energy of its particles

questions.explanation: Temperature is an average over the particles: it measures how fast, on average, they are moving. It does not depend on how many particles there are, and it is not itself a form of energy that is transferred.

questions.stem: Solid ammonium nitrate is dissolved in water in a polystyrene cup, and the temperature of the water falls from 21.0 °C to 15.5 °C. Which statement explains the fall in temperature?

options.text: Energy is transferred from the water to the dissolving solid, so the process is endothermic.
The solution is the system; it loses energy, so its temperature falls and the process is exothermic.
Cold is released by the dissolving solid and spreads out through all of the water in the polystyrene cup.
Energy is used up as the solid dissolves, so the total energy of everything decreases.

questions.stem: The energy profile of an endothermic reaction is sketched with reaction coordinate on the x-axis and potential energy on the y-axis. Which statement about this profile is correct?

options.text: The products are more stable than the reactants, as they have more energy.
It shows an energy barrier, which the profile of an exothermic reaction lacks.
The products are at a higher potential energy than the reactants.
The distance along the x-axis shows how long the reaction takes.

questions.explanation: In an endothermic reaction the system gains energy from the surroundings, so the products end at a higher potential energy than the reactants. The difference between the two levels is ΔH, which is positive.

questions.stem: A spirit burner containing ethanol, C₂H₅OH, is used to heat 150.0 g of water in a copper can. Burning 0.920 g of ethanol raises the temperature of the water from 19.0 °C to 40.5 °C. Use c(water) = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ and A_r values H 1.01, C 12.01, O 16.00. What value of ΔH for the combustion of ethanol do these results give?

options.text: −6.75 × 10⁵ kJ mol⁻¹
−6.75 × 10² kJ mol⁻¹
−9.25 × 10³ kJ mol⁻¹
−1.35 × 10¹ kJ mol⁻¹

questions.stem: Methane burns in oxygen: CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(g). The reaction is exothermic. Which statement explains why?

options.text: Forming the bonds in CO₂ and H₂O releases more energy than breaking the bonds in CH₄ and O₂ absorbs.
Breaking the bonds in CH₄ and O₂ releases the stored energy, which passes to the surroundings.
More bonds are formed in CO₂ and H₂O than are broken in CH₄ and O₂, so energy is released.
The energy is stored in the CH₄; the O₂ only lets it be released and has no part in the change.

questions.explanation: Breaking the C–H and O=O bonds absorbs energy; forming the C=O and O–H bonds releases energy. Because the bonds formed are stronger in total, more energy is released than absorbed, and the difference is transferred to the surroundings.

questions.stem: Use the enthalpy changes of reactions 1 and 2 to calculate ΔH for the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide: 2H₂O₂(l) → 2H₂O(l) + O₂(g). Reaction 1: H₂(g) + O₂(g) → H₂O₂(l), ΔH₁ = −187.8 kJ mol⁻¹. Reaction 2: 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l), ΔH₂ = −571.6 kJ mol⁻¹.

options.text: −947.2 kJ mol⁻¹
+196.0 kJ mol⁻¹
−383.8 kJ mol⁻¹
−196.0 kJ mol⁻¹

questions.explanation: Reverse reaction 1 and double it: 2H₂O₂(l) → 2H₂(g) + 2O₂(g), ΔH = −2ΔH₁ = +375.6 kJ mol⁻¹. Add reaction 2 (ΔH₂ = −571.6 kJ mol⁻¹): 2H₂ and one O₂ cancel, leaving the target. ΔH = +375.6 − 571.6 = −196.0 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: The boiling points of four successive alcohols are: methanol 65 °C, ethanol 78 °C, propan-1-ol 97 °C and butan-1-ol 118 °C. Which statement explains this trend?

options.text: Longer molecules have more H atoms, so they form more hydrogen bonds.
Longer molecules contain more covalent bonds to break on boiling.
Heavier molecules need more energy to move, whatever the forces.
London forces grow with chain length; each molecule still has one –OH group.

questions.explanation: Each molecule has one –OH group, so hydrogen bonding per molecule is similar across the series. Each extra CH₂ adds electrons and contact area, strengthening the London forces between molecules, so more energy is needed to separate them.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CHO?

options.text: 3-methylbutanal
2-methylbutanol
2-methylbutanal
2-ethylpropanal

questions.explanation: The longest chain containing the –CHO carbon has four carbon atoms (butanal). The –CHO carbon is carbon 1, so the methyl branch is on carbon 2: 2-methylbutanal.

questions.stem: Which compound is a tertiary alcohol?

options.text: CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₂CH₃
CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂OH
HOCH₂CH(OH)CH₂OH
(CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂CH₃

questions.explanation: In 2-methylbutan-2-ol the carbon carrying –OH is bonded to three other carbon atoms (two CH₃ groups and a CH₂CH₃ group), so it is a tertiary alcohol.

questions.stem: Magnesium ribbon is added to dilute hydrochloric acid in an insulated cup, and the temperature of the solution rises. Which statement correctly describes the energy changes?

options.text: Energy is created by the reaction, so the total energy of the system and the surroundings increases.
The reacting chemicals gain energy, and the rise in the temperature of the solution shows this.
The energy of the reacting chemicals falls by exactly the same amount as the energy of the surroundings rises.
Temperature is transferred from the reacting chemicals to the water, which is why the water warms up.

questions.stem: An energy profile for a reaction is plotted with reaction coordinate on the x-axis and potential energy on the y-axis. Relative to the same zero, the reactants are at 150 kJ mol⁻¹, the top of the energy barrier is at 280 kJ mol⁻¹ and the products are at 40 kJ mol⁻¹. What is ΔH for the reaction?

options.text: −110 kJ mol⁻¹
+110 kJ mol⁻¹
+130 kJ mol⁻¹
−240 kJ mol⁻¹

questions.explanation: ΔH = potential energy of products − potential energy of reactants = 40 − 150 = −110 kJ mol⁻¹. The products lie below the reactants, so the reaction is exothermic and ΔH is negative.

questions.stem:
50.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ HCl(aq) is placed in a polystyrene cup and 25.0 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ NaOH(aq) is added. The temperature of the mixture rises by 4.50 °C.
HCl(aq) + NaOH(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l)
Assume that the solutions have a density of 1.00 g cm⁻³ and a specific heat capacity of 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹. What is ΔH for the reaction?

options.text: −28.2 kJ mol⁻¹
−37.6 kJ mol⁻¹
−1.41 kJ mol⁻¹
−56.4 kJ mol⁻¹

questions.stem: Which compound can exist as cis and trans isomers?

options.text: 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene
1,3-dichloropropane
2-bromo-3-methylbutane
1,2-dimethylcyclobutane

questions.explanation: The ring restricts rotation, and carbons 1 and 2 each carry two different groups (a CH₃ group and an H atom). The two CH₃ groups can be on the same side (cis) or opposite sides (trans) of the ring.

questions.stem: Which statement about the molecular ion peak in the mass spectrum of an organic compound is correct?

options.text: It is the tallest peak, as most molecules reach the detector unbroken.
It is due to an ion formed when a molecule gains an electron.
Any peak at lower m/z than it shows an impurity in the sample.
Its m/z value gives the relative molecular mass of the compound.

questions.explanation: The molecular ion, M⁺, is the whole molecule minus one electron. With a charge of 1+, its m/z value equals the relative molecular mass of the compound.

questions.stem: A compound, C₃H₆O₂, has an IR spectrum with a very broad absorption across 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ and a strong absorption at 1715 cm⁻¹. Characteristic ranges: O–H (alcohols) 3200–3600 cm⁻¹; O–H (carboxylic acids) 2500–3000 cm⁻¹; C–H 2850–3090 cm⁻¹; C=O 1700–1750 cm⁻¹; C=C 1620–1680 cm⁻¹. Which interpretation is correct?

options.text: It is an alcohol: the broad band is the O–H of a hydroxyl group.
It is an ester: the 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ band is due only to C–H bonds.
It is a carboxylic acid: there is a broad acid O–H band and a C=O band.
It has a C=C bond, which causes the absorption at 1715 cm⁻¹.

questions.explanation: A very broad band across 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ is the O–H of a carboxylic acid, and 1715 cm⁻¹ lies in the C=O range, 1700–1750 cm⁻¹. The compound is propanoic acid, CH₃CH₂COOH.

questions.stem: Which describes the ¹H NMR spectrum of 2-methylpropan-2-ol, (CH₃)₃COH?

options.text: one signal, as only H atoms on carbon give signals
two signals, with areas in the ratio 1:1
two signals, whose areas are in the ratio 9:1
ten signals, one for each H atom in the molecule

questions.explanation: The nine hydrogen atoms of the three equivalent CH₃ groups form one environment, and the O–H hydrogen forms a second. Two signals, with areas in the ratio 9:1.

questions.stem: In the ¹H NMR spectrum of butanone, CH₃COCH₂CH₃, which splitting pattern does the signal from the CH₃ group bonded to the carbonyl carbon show?

options.text: a quartet, as the CH₃ group itself contains three H atoms
a singlet, as the adjacent carbon has no H atoms
a doublet, as its carbon is bonded to one other carbon atom
a triplet, as it is split by the two H atoms of the CH₂ group

questions.explanation: The only carbon adjacent to this CH₃ group is the carbonyl carbon, which has no hydrogen atoms. With n = 0 neighbouring H atoms, the signal is a singlet (n + 1 = 1).

questions.stem: Which compound has a chiral carbon atom?

options.text: propan-2-ol
butan-2-ol
but-2-ene
chloroethane

questions.explanation: Carbon 2 of butan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, is bonded to four different groups: H, OH, CH₃ and CH₂CH₃. The molecule is therefore chiral and exists as a pair of enantiomers.
